name: Rotary
keywords: telephone rotary dial pop desk phone
idea: The site is a pillar-box-red desk phone on cobalt wallpaper. The dial is the navigation: every extension reaches something, and 0 is the operator (contact).
note: Live: tap any hole (or Tab to it and press Enter). The full lab version also supports dragging the hole round to the stop.
borrowed: Mid-century desk telephones: the clear finger wheel over a printed number card, the chrome finger stop, pulse dialling as the wheel returns, the directory card, plus 1960s pop-art colour and a patterned wallpaper behind.
mood: Loud, witty, tactile. Suits playful personal sites, creative agencies, events and campaigns. Wrong for serious B2B or dense documentation.

patterns.css: background:radial-gradient(circle 12px at 0 50%,#1A35D1 98%,transparent) left/51% 100% no-repeat,radial-gradient(circle 12px at 100% 50%,#1A35D1 98%,transparent) right/51% 100% no-repeat,#FFD23F
patterns.label: Ticket notches

motion: Hole k sits at 60 − 30k degrees; it needs 60 + 30k degrees of rotation to reach the stop at 120°.
Return is linear (a governor), ~180ms + 950ms × rotation/330, emitting one pulse per digit (0 = 10).
Phone shakes while ringing; handset lifts on connect; content lines rise in with a stagger.
Typing a digit anywhere dials it.
watchouts: Provide a plain directory list too: never make the dial the only route.
Red on cobalt vibrates. Separate them with ivory or a deep shadow.
Sound (pulse clicks, ring) stays off until the visitor turns the ringer on.
